text: This Paper 1 question uses data about ticket sales at ballet performances. Students complete a grouped frequency table, identify the modal class, read a cumulative frequency curve, discuss sampling methods, interpret a box-and-whisker diagram, and calculate the effect of adding 18 tickets to every performance on the mean and variance.

stem_blocks.text: A ballet company performs The Sleeping Beauty every year. Last year they gave a total of 60 performances at their theatre which has a maximum capacity of 800. The number of tickets sold, n, at each performance is shown in a grouped frequency table.
The following cumulative frequency diagram also displays these data.

After a performance, the company decides to conduct a survey to obtain feedback from the audience. Last year 36000 tickets were sold to The Sleeping Beauty. A box and whisker diagram displays the amount spent by the audience at the souvenir shop when they attended the performance.

stem_blocks.text: Two friends Amelia and Bill, each set themselves a target of saving $20000. They each have $9000 to invest.

Amelia invests her $9000 in an account that offers an interest rate of 7% per annum compounded annually. Bill invests his $9000 in an account that offers an interest rate of r% per annum compounded monthly, where r is set to two decimal places. A third friend Chris also wants to reach the $20000 target. He puts his money in a safe where he does not earn any interest. His system is to add more money to this safe each year. Each year he will add half the amount added in the previous year.

solution.outline: For Amelia, use annual compound interest: 9000(1+0.07)^5=12622.965..., so the value is $12600 to the nearest hundred, and solving 9000(1+0.07)^x=20000 gives 12 years. For Bill, solve 9000(1+r/(100*12))^(12*10)=20000 to obtain r=8.01170..., so the minimum two-decimal-place rate is 8.02%. For Chris, the yearly additions form a geometric series with ratio 1/2. With initial deposit 9000, the infinite sum is 9000/(1-0.5)=18000, so the target is never reached. To reach the target after 5 years, solve u_1(1-0.5^5)/0.5=20000, giving u_1=10322.58..., so $10323.

blocks.text: Find the value of c.
Determine whether this lottery is a fair game in the first week. Justify your answer.

answers.text: Interchanging x and y in y=(4x+1)/(x+4) and solving for y gives f^(-1)(x)=(1-4x)/(x-4).
A reflection in the y-axis gives f(-x)=(-4x+1)/(-x+4). Reflecting this result in the x-axis gives -f(-x)=-( -4x+1)/(-x+4)=(1-4x)/(x-4)=f^(-1)(x), as required.
Solving f(x)=f^(-1)(x) gives p=-1 and q=1.
The enclosed area is integral from -1 to 1 of ((4x+1)/(x+4)-(1-4x)/(x-4)) dx, which is 0.675231..., so the area is 0.675.

rows.text: Method 1: recognizes that g(x) is the integral of 3x^2 + 5e^x. Integrating gives g(x) = x^3 + 5e^x + C, with one A1 for each integrated term. text: An engineer is designing an open-top rainwater gutter from sheet metal 45 cm wide and 600 cm long. stem_blocks.text: An engineer is designing a gutter to catch rainwater from the roof of a house.
The gutter will be open at the top and is made by folding a piece of sheet metal 45 cm wide and 600 cm long.

The cross-section of the gutter is shaded in the diagram. The height of both vertical sides is 10 cm. The width of the gutter is w cm. Arc AB lies on the circumference of a circle with centre O and radius 12 cm.
Let angle AOB = theta radians, where 0 < theta < pi.

In a storm, the total volume, in cm^3, of rainwater that enters the gutter can be modelled by R(t), where t is the time in seconds since the start of the storm. The rate is R'(t)=50 cos(2pi t/5)+3000 for t>=0.
During any 60-second period, if the volume of rainwater entering the gutter is greater than the volume of the gutter, it will overflow.

blocks.text: Show that theta=2.08, correct to three significant figures.
Find the area of the cross-section of the gutter.
Determine whether the gutter overflowed in this storm. Justify your answer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that theta=2.08, correct to three significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the cross-section of the gutter.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine whether the gutter overflowed in this storm. Justify your answer.

answers.text: The curved arc length is 45-10-10=25 cm, so 25=12theta and theta=25/12=2.08 to three significant figures.
Using theta=2.08, w=2(12)sin(theta/2)=20.7 cm. The cross-sectional area is the rectangle 10w plus the circular segment area, giving approximately 294 cm^2.

The gutter volume is about 600 times the cross-sectional area, approximately 176000 cm^3. In any 60-second period the rainfall volume is integral of R'(t), equal to 180000 cm^3 because the cosine term completes whole periods. Since 180000 is greater than the gutter volume, the gutter overflowed.

Uses the determined normal distribution to evaluate the upper-tail probability at 26 mm. P(X>26)=0.106. Models Y as binomial with n=10 and p=0.10621… . Forms E(Y)=10×0.10621… . E(Y)=1.06. Evaluates P(Y=3) from the binomial distribution. P(Y=3)=0.0655. Recognizes conditional probability given X<26. Forms 0.3554/(1−0.10621…). Conditional probability=0.398.
